reasoning:
**CRM-35 adds a literal-string guard to enforce i18n discipline.** The story's three pieces of work are:
1. A grammar-aware static check that scans `web/src/pages/**` and `web/src/features/**` for hardcoded user-facing strings, failing the build with file and line number.
2. Type-safe key equality: confirm TypeScript's `Messages` type prevents missing keys, identify what it misses (e.g., extra keys), and close the gap at build time.
3. Verify no positional dictionary indexing (no `Object.values(t)[n]`).

**Plan-lessons first** (explicit mandate in hints): `.squad/plan-lessons.md` contains 16 defects to avoid. The intake warns specifically about L-13 (false positives in literal guards—scope it narrowly to JSX text nodes and text-rendering props only, not imports/classNames/routes/test-ids) and L-16 (prove the guard fails by adding a violation, seeing the error, reverting).

**Acceptance criteria and rule**: `scripts/criteria/languages.md` and `scripts/rules.txt` specify BR-6 and the four hard requirements (no hardcoded strings, key-set equality, both-language updates in one change, lookup by key not position).

**Existing i18n** (shipped in CRM-25, must not rebuild): `web/src/shared/i18n/` contains the provider, context, `useTranslation()` hook, and both resource files. Both pages already read through it. The guard integrates with this, not replaces it.

**Key-matching test**: `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` asserts `Object.keys(en) === Object.keys(ar)`. The plan must audit: does this catch an extra key in `ar` not in `en` (likely not—it tests reference equality, not set equality). Close that gap.

**Pages to scan** (must see real examples): `HomePage` and `SignInPage` illustrate what the guard targets.

**Components to exclude** (must clarify the boundary): `Button` and `Text` in `shared/ui/` take text as props and must NOT be flagged. The story explicitly warns that scanning the UI module would create false positives.

**Test harness**: `web/src/testing/render.tsx` already supports `language: 'ar'`. New tests use this.

**Build integration**: `web/package.json` shows existing scripts; the plan adds a build-time guard (likely a new script or a build-step plugin). `web/vite.config.ts` and `web/tsconfig.json` may need updates.

**Conventions**: `docs/architecture.md`, `docs/git.md`, and `docs/taxonomy.md` establish naming and structure.

**Suggested strategy**: `read_full` — all files are small (≤ 11.7 KB) and all are critical to understanding the scope, boundary, and integration points.

delta: # Story 01 — Web resource-file guard and matching-key check (Story:

CRM-35)

## Prerequisites

- PLATFORM-10-WEB shipped `web/src/shared/i18n/` (`en.ts`, `
ar.ts`, `index.tsx` with `I18nProvider`/`useTranslation`) and `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` already asserts the two key sets match —

**do not rebuild any of that**.
- PLATFORM-9-WEB (the web-root scaffolding this story depends on per the

intake) is on `main`; nothing in this plan changes routing, primitives, or provider wiring.
- C
RM-26 web test harness (`web/src/testing/render.tsx` — `renderWithProviders(ui, { language: 'ar' })`) is in place and

used by existing tests.
- Read `.squad/plan-lessons.md` first — in particular **L-13** (a

source-scanning guard must read grammar, not prose) and **L-16** (prove the guard fails before believing it passes).

---

## Story Goal

Close the three
real gaps left after PLATFORM-10-WEB so BR-6 ("two languages, always, in resource files, never

hardcoded") is enforced, not merely observed:

1. Add a **narrow, grammar-aware** guard that fails the test suite when a page or feature source contains a user-facing string
literal (JSX text nodes and the specific props that render user-visible text). Scope: `web/src/pages/**

` and `web/src/features/**` only.
2. Close the one gap left by TypeScript's structural typing of `Messages`: a **
key present in `ar.ts` but not in `en.ts`** (an extra Arabic key) currently passes `tsc`. Turn that into a build failure via
the type system, so the second criterion ("build failure rather than a blank on a screen") is met at compile time and not just by a

runtime test.
3. Prove strings are looked up **by key**: assert that no page code indexes the dictionary positionally (

`Object.values(t)[n]`, `Object.keys(t)[n]`, numeric brackets on `t`).

Out of scope (and stated so a
later story does not re-litigate): no i18next, no formatjs, no runtime language switching (LANGUAGES-2-WEB), no locale-

aware date/number formatting (LANGUAGES-3-WEB), no cross-root missing-key check (LANGUAGES-4-ALL), no re-translation of the provisional Arabic text.

---

## Context

— Read These Files First

1. `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` — full file (25 lines). The `en` object with s
ections `signIn` and `home`, and the `Messages` mapped type on lines 23–25 that widens values to `string` on

purpose. Note the comment on lines 19–22 explaining why `as const` is **not** used.
2. `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` — full file (19 lines). `export const ar: Messages = { …
}`. This is what causes a missing key in `ar.ts` to already fail `tsc`; verify it, and note

the gap: an **extra** property in `ar.ts` still satisfies `Messages` structurally.
3. `web/src/shared/i18n/index.tsx` — full file (46 lines). `I18nProvider`

(lines 18–40) and `useTranslation()` (lines 42–46). Do not change the reader.
4. `web/src/pages/home
/HomePage.tsx` — full file (22 lines). Every string already comes from `t.home.*`. Use this as the reference for "clean" page gr

ammar the guard must accept.
5. `web/src/pages/sign-in/SignInPage.tsx` — full file (57 lines). Note the mix of JSX text
(`{t.signIn.heading}`), text-carrying props (`label={t.signIn.emailLabel}`) and **non-text** attributes the guard must ignore (`id

="email"`, `name="email"`, `type="email"`, `autoComplete="username"`, `type="password"`, `type="submit"`, `autoComplete="current-password"`).
6. `web/src/shared/ui/primit
ives.test.tsx` — lines 65–76. Existing key-set equality test (`flatten(ar).sort()).toEqual(flatten(en).sort())`) and the "act

ually different text" test. Match its style; do **not** duplicate the equality test.
7. `web/src/testing/render.tsx` — full file (47 lines). The harness the

tests should keep using.
8. `web/package.json` — full file. Confirms **Vitest 4**, TypeScript 7, no i

18n library. `test` script is `vitest run`, `typecheck` is `tsc -b --noEmit`, `build` is `tsc -b && vite build`.
9. `scripts/criteria/langu

ages.md` — section `## LANGUAGES-1-WEB` (lines 11–31). The four acceptance criteria this plan implements.
10. `scrip

ts/rules.txt` line 10 — BR-6, verbatim.
11. `.squad/plan-lessons.md` — sections **L-13** (lines 169–181) and **L-16** (line 208+). The
literal-scan test in `primitives.test.tsx` at lines 45–63 is the local precedent for how to strip com

ments before scanning source.
12. Grep for existing dictionary access patterns before writing the "by key" assertion: `` grep -rE

n "Object\.(values|keys)\(t\)|\bt\[[0-9]" web/src/pages web/src/features ``.

---

## Product rules (from story

)

- **Current behaviour.** Both pages read every string through `useTranslation()`. `Messages` makes a **missing** key in `ar.ts` a compile error. A runtime test verif
ies key-set equality. Nothing stops the next page from typing a JSX literal, and an **extra** key in `ar.ts` compiles cl

ean.
- **New behaviour.** A page or feature source that contains a user-facing string literal fails a test that names the file and the line. An extra key in `ar.ts`

that `en.ts` does not have fails `tsc`. Positional dictionary access in page/feature code fails a test.

---

## Implementation tasks

No backend changes required

. No new runtime dependency. All changes live under `web/`.

### 1 — Close the "extra key" gap in the resource-file types

**

File: `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts`** (edit lines 23–25).

The current `Messages` type widens values but does **not** constrain the
section keys to those declared in `en`. TypeScript's structural subtyping means an object with an **additional** section on `ar` still satisfies `Messages
`. Tighten the type so any section key on `ar` must also be a section key on `en`, and any leaf key inside a

section must exist on the same `en` section. Keep values widened to `string` (the reason on lines 19–22 still holds).

Concretely, repl

ace the `Messages` type with a shape that:
- Uses `keyof typeof en` as the exact section-key set (already true).
- Ad
ds a companion type used by `ar.ts` that requires the **same section keys and the same leaf keys** — no more, no less — with

`string` values. This is what closes the "extra key in `ar`" gap.

Suggested shape (executor may keep names but must
ras. `Exact` uses an intersection with a "no other keys" clause so
a simpler formulation covers **both** the extra-section and extra-leaf-key case with the current TS 7
checker, prefer it. What must be true after the edit: adding `foo: 'bar'` at the top of `ar` **or** in

side `ar.signIn` fails `pnpm --dir web typecheck`.

**File: `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`** (edit line 1 and line 7).

Change

the imported type and the annotation from `Messages` to `Locale` (or whatever the new stricter alias is named):

```ts
import type { Locale } from './

but adjust the wording to reflect that **both** a missing key and an extra key are now compile errors.

### 2 — Add the literal guard as a Vitest test

**

Create file: `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.**

Location rationale: colocated with the sources it guards; pic

ked up automatically by `vitest run`; ignored by production builds.

What the test does:

- Walk `web/src/pages/
**/*.{ts,tsx}` and `web/src/features/**/*.{ts,tsx}` (the latter directory may not yet exist — `fs.existsSync` it and sk
ip when absent). **Exclude** anything ending in `.test.ts`, `.test.tsx`, `.spec.ts`, `.spec.tsx`, `.stories.tsx`.
- For each file, strip `/* … */` and `// …` comments the same way `primitives.test.tsx` line 48 does. Also strip TypeScript string-
literal types (e.g. `type X = 'foo' | 'bar'`) is not required — the productions below already exclude non-J

SX contexts.
- Parse the source and flag **only** these two productions as user-facing literals:
  1. **JSX text nodes**: text
between an opening JSX tag and its close that is not whitespace, is not entirely `{…}` expression, and is not inside a `<script>` or `<style>`

(none of those exist in pages today).
  2. **String literals passed to a JSX attribute whose name is in a small allow-list of
text-carrying props**: `aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-valuetext`, `placeholder`, `title`

, `alt`. When the attribute value is a JSX expression (`{…}`) it is fine; when it is a raw string literal (`title="Sign in"`) it is a violation.
- What the
guard **must not** flag (state each explicitly in a comment at the top of

the test, for L-13):
  - Import paths (`from '../../shared/ui'`).
  - `className` values.
  - Route strings (`navigate('/',

…)`).
  - Test ids and non-text HTML attributes: `id`, `name`, `type`, `autoComplete`, `htmlFor`, `role

`, `data-*`, `key`, `href`, `src`, `rel`, `target`.
  - String-literal **types** (`type Language = 'en' | 'ar'`

) and string-literal **union return values**.
  - Anything inside a `/* i18n-ignore */` block-comment (escape hatch for the rare case a

future story finds; document it, but do not use it in current sources).

**Grammar, not prose (

L-13).** Use a real parser, not regex over source text. Options in order of preference:
1. **TypeScript's own AST** via the
`typescript` package — it is already a transitive dependency (via `typescript` itself, listed in `web/package.json` line 27). Use `ts.createSourceFile(file, code
, ts.ScriptTarget.Latest, /*setParentNodes*/ true, ts.ScriptKind.T

SX)` and visit `JsxText`, `JsxAttribute` and `StringLiteral` nodes. This adds no npm dependency.
2. If,
when the executor tries option 1, the installed `typescript` version does not export the visitor helpers needed, fall back to `@babel/parser` + `@babel/traverse

` — but only if step 1 is genuinely unworkable. Prefer option 1.

Report format when the test fails: one
line per violation, `path/to/file.tsx:LINE:COLUMN — <production>:

<literal>`. Then `expect(violations).toEqual([])`.

**Prove it fails (L-16).** In the same test file, add a second test that constructs a tiny in

-memory TSX string containing:
- a JSX text node (`<Heading level={1}>Sign in</Heading>`),
- an

offending `title` attribute (`<button title="Go">…</button>`),
- a benign `type="submit"` and `className="x"`

and `id="email"`.

Run the same walker against the in-memory source (pass a fake filename) and assert that exactly the two off
ending literals are flagged and the three benign strings are not. This is the "prove it fails" seat-belt required by L-16, and it keeps the walker's

grammar under test forever.

### 3 — Add the "by key" assertion

**Add to `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`**
a third test that, for every file the walker considers (same glob, same exclusions), asserts none of these patterns appear (ra

w regex over the comment-stripped source is fine here — the shape is unambiguous):

- `Object.values(t)` or `Object.entries(t)` when the rece

iver is the translation object.
- `Object.keys(t)[` followed by anything.
- Numeric index into `

t` itself: `t[0]`, `t[1]`, … (regex: `\bt\[\s*\d`).

Failure message: `<file>:<line> — dictionary acc

essed by index or position; use t.section.key`.

### 4 — Do not touch existing key-set equality test

Leave `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` lines 65–76 alone
. The runtime equality test is now a belt over the type suspenders; it stays because it also catches a hand-edit

ing mistake in `ar.ts` that a broken build would otherwise mask.

### 5 — Documentation stub inside the test file

At the top of `web/src/pages/no

-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`, keep a comment (10–15 lines) that:
- Names BR-6 and `scripts/rules.txt` line 10.

- Lists the two productions the guard judges (JSX text; the eight text-carrying props).
- Lists the categories the guard deliberately ignores (className, route

, id/name/type/autoComplete/htmlFor/role/data-*, imports, string-literal types).
- Notes the `/* i18n-ignore */` escape hatch.
- Points at

`scripts/criteria/languages.md#LANGUAGES-1-WEB`.

No AI-assistance mention anywhere.

---

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

-
**Empty page directory.** If `web/src/features/` does not exist, the walker returns `[]` for that root and the test still

runs against `web/src/pages/`. Enforced by `fs.existsSync` before `readdirSync`.
- **Only-whitespace JSX text
.** `<Card>   \n   <Heading …/></Card>` must not flag. Enforced by `text.trim() === ''` before treating a `JsxText` node as

a literal.
- **JSX expression that happens to be a string literal.** `<Heading>{'Sign in'}</Heading>` — a `JsxExpression` wrapping a `StringLiteral`
. The guard **must** flag it; otherwise the escape hatch is a one-character workaround. Enforced by inspecting `JsxExpression` children and matching a

bare `StringLiteral`.
- **Unicode text.** Arabic literals (`title="مرحبا"`) must be flagged the same way as English ones. Enforced by

matching on node kind, not on character range.
- **String-literal type on a page.** `type Variant = 'primary' | 'secondary'` in a page file must not flag. Enforced because such nodes are `

LiteralType`/`TypeAliasDeclaration`, never `JsxText` or `JsxAttribute`.
- **JSX attribute expression.** `title

={t.foo.bar}` must not flag: the attribute value is a `JsxExpression`, not a `StringLiteral`.
- **Numeric access to `t` inside a com

ment.** Comment stripping happens first; a comment containing `t[0]` is discarded before the "by key" scan.
- **Extra
key in `ar.ts`.** After Task 1, adding `extraSection: { foo: 'x' }` at the top of `ar` must break `tsc`. Verified in

Verification Step 3.
- **Missing key in `ar.ts`.** Already a compile error today via `Messages`; must remain so after the type change.
- **A future page under a nested directory.** The walker recurses; verified because it uses `readdirSync(..., { withFileTypes: true,
recursive: true })` (or a manual recursion — recursive option is on Node 20+, which the api

tests use; the web tests run under the same Node).
- **`Object.values(en)` outside a page file.** Only files

under `pages/` and `features/` are scanned, so PLATFORM tests using `flatten(en)` are not affected.
- **Escape hatch abused
.** `/* i18n-ignore */` is honored per-line; document that a plan review rejects a page that ad

ds one without a rule-owner sign-off. No source uses it today.

---

## Test Plan

1

. **New:** `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts` — three tests:
   - `pages and features hold no user-facing string literal

` (walks the real filesystem; expects `[]`).
   - `the walker flags exactly the two productions it is meant to` (runs against an in-memory TSX fixture; asserts the two se

eded violations and none of the benign strings — this is the L-16 "prove it fails" test).
   - `pages and features look strings up by key, not by index` (walks the

real filesystem; expects `[]`).
2. **Unchanged, must still pass:** `web/src/shared/ui/primitives.test.tsx` lines 16–76, including the key-set equality test at

lines 65–76.
3. **Unchanged, must still pass:** every test currently under `web/src/**` (30 tests today per the intake).
4. **Type
-check test:** none as a Vitest case — the type is enforced by `pnpm --dir web typecheck` and by `pnpm --dir

web build`. See Verification Step 3.

---

## Migration / Rollback

Not a migration. If the guard is too aggressive in review, the shortest revert is:
1

. Remove `web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts`.
2. Revert the `Messages` → `Locale` rename in `web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts` and `web/src/shared/i18n/

ar.ts`.

No data, no configuration, no on-disk state is touched. There is no partial-migration state to guard against.

---

## Verification Steps

1. **Web tests p

ass:** `pnpm --dir web test` — 30 existing tests + the 3 new ones (33 total) all pass.
2. **Web build succeeds:** `pnpm --dir web build` — `tsc -b && vite build` fin

ishes without errors, proving the stricter `Locale` type still admits `ar.ts` as written today.
3. **Prove the type gap is clos
ed (L-16):** temporarily add `foo: 'bar'` at the top of `web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts`; run `pnpm --dir web typecheck`; expect a compile error naming `foo`;

revert. Do the same by adding `nonExistent: 'x'` inside `ar.signIn`; expect a compile error naming `nonExistent`; revert.
4. **
Prove the literal guard fires (L-16):** temporarily add `<Heading level={1}>Sign in</Heading>` (raw string) to `web/src/pages/home/HomePage.tsx`; run `pnpm --dir web test`
; expect the new test to fail with `web/src/pages/home/HomePage.tsx:<line>:<col> — JSX text: Sign in`. Revert. Rep

eat with `<Button title="Go">…</Button>` on `SignInPage.tsx`; expect a `title` violation; revert.
5. **Prove the by-key guard fires (L-16):**
temporarily change `HomePage.tsx` line 14 to `Object.values(t)[0]`; expect the by-key test to fail with a message that names the file and line. Revert.

6. **Regression — API untouched:** `pnpm --dir api test` — the 82 API tests still pass; no file under `api/` was edited.
7. **No AI attribution anywhere
new:** `grep -RniE "(claude|copilot|chatgpt|gpt-|openai|anthropic|ai[-

]generated|ai assistance)" web/src/pages/no-hardcoded-strings.test.ts web/src/shared/i18n/en.ts web/src/shared/i18n/ar.ts` returns no matches.
8. **Conf

irm no new npm dependency:** `git diff web/package.json web/package-lock.json` shows no additions in `dependencies` or `devDependencies`.

---

## Done Cri

(`aria-label`, `aria-description`, `aria-placeholder`, `aria-roledescription`, `aria-valuetext`, `placeholder`, `title`, `alt`).
- [ ] The same test file includes an in-memory fixture test
